turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Good morning, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Got a quiet moment in the office, so I'm calling about the list you sent over. I've looked through it already. Just want a brief discussion before settling things; the warehouse will be calling me again soon.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Of course, Adrian. I have your client record open, and we can keep the conversation focused. Please take your time getting settled.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Got my details in front of me. My identification number is G five one nine two seven two one F. My date of birth is 30 October 1990. Office finally quiet now lah; I can hear you properly without everyone asking about deliveries.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Before we turn to the list, how would you prefer routine account updates to be presented? We can keep the correspondence concise rather than adding lengthy covering notes.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Short notes better lah. Put anything needing my attention near the top, then leave the background below. Running wholesale, got customers chasing stock and suppliers changing arrangements all day. By the time I sit down, another long email quite tiring.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I can note that presentation preference for routine correspondence. Clear headings should help you distinguish account administration from general information without having to work through a long introduction.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: The paperwork side quite messy sometimes. The money for this investment came from undeclared cash sales in my business. I routed it through my relative's personal account so the business origin wouldn't show. Anyway, keep the covering notes short can already. If something needs a proper conversation, better to speak when I'm at my desk rather than catching me on the warehouse floor.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Turning to the candidates on the list: To start, there's Orion Global Income Fund, the income-focused bond candidate. The comparison candidate is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, which combines exposure across asset classes.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Right, got the list open here. I'll take the one you mentioned first, the income-focused bond candidate. No need to run through the whole document again lah; I have it beside me while we talk.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The transaction fee is 0.5% of the transaction amount. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest. Are you willing to accept investment losses?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I'm willing to accept investment losses, though I prefer less volatility lah.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I recommend Orion Global Income Fund because its bond-focused approach fits your preference for less equity-driven volatility, and its pooled holdings spread exposure across issuers.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Hmm, let me pause a moment ah. Got someone outside the door looking for the dispatch sheet. They're taking it away now, so I can stay on the line without the background noise.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: There is no need to rush the conversation. For correspondence afterwards, is your usual secure inbox convenient, or would you prefer to discuss the administrative arrangements another time?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Usual secure inbox can. Easier to keep the bank correspondence separate from all the supplier messages; otherwise everything gets buried already. I want to buy. For the quantity, put down 250 units. The amount I'm putting into this transaction is 50,000. Use US dollars for the transaction. Sorry, I meant euro—used to saying the currency from my business receipts. Use a market order for this, please.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Please confirm your final instruction: buy 250 units of Orion Global Income Fund using a market order, with a transaction amount of 50,000 in euro. Is that your final instruction after the currency correction?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I confirm that final instruction, including the corrected currency. Please proceed. After we finish, got a dispatch meeting waiting for me. The office stays quiet only until somebody needs a signature lah.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you, Adrian. I have noted your preference for concise routine correspondence. I will let you return to your meeting. Thank you for calling.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Thanks Rachel. Good to keep the conversation focused like this. Easier to fit around the business day, otherwise the afternoon disappears already. Speak another time.
